description:
The user chose to land this before fz-mue.12, relayed by Elixir Parity on 2026-11-19. Owner: Elixir Parity. A proposal page comes first.

## Why
Elixir code builds hygienic variables from helper functions and from atom contexts. For example, Record.__access__ is a helper function that hoists values through Macro.unique_var(key, module). fz rejects both forms:
1. {:x, [counter: 7], Gen} fails with "a variable's context atom must be nil or generated, got Elixir.Gen".
2. A variable written by quote inside a helper function that a macro calls fails with "a macro- or sugar-generated variable is missing its hygiene ordinal". Only the invoked macro's own quotes are stamped (stamp_hygiene, quoted_expander.rs).

## Done when
- Macro.var/2 and Macro.unique_var/2 exist.
- Atom-context variables are hygienic per Elixir's rules: context and counter.
- Quotes in helper functions are hygienic.
- Elixir-oracle fixtures pass on all three paths.

## Related
fz-p8p.25 (var!/2) needs the same decision this ticket makes: what a context atom denotes. p8p.25 builds on this answer and does not make it again.

comments.text: Proposal page /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-mue.38.html awaits the user. Elixir's rule: a context atom names a variable namespace. Identity is {name,counter} or {name,context}. quote writes its module atom. An expansion stamps counter {CallerModule, ordinal} on its own module's variables, helpers included. var!(v,M) deletes the counter and sets the context (= p8p.25).

title: A macro's variables are hygienic wherever they are written: atom-context variables, Macro.var/2 and Macro.unique_var/2, and quotes in helper functions
